text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.7% today, extending a two-week decline of 14%, as oil prices remain under pressure and refinery margins tighten. US crude is trading at $89.53 per barrel while refineries are running at 95.7% capacity—high utilization combined with moderating oil prices squeezes the profit refiners make on each barrel processed. Gasoline and diesel inventories are building (215.9 million and 104.9 million barrels respectively), adding to margin pressure as supply outpaces demand signals.

Geopolitical disruptions—Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, mine strikes on tankers in the Hormuz Strait, and ongoing Ukraine-Russia refinery attacks—have failed to sustainably lift oil prices, suggesting markets expect these supply risks to remain contained or that demand concerns are outweighing them. This backdrop of persistent margin compression, despite headline geopolitical risk, is likely keeping downward pressure on refinery stocks.
